$comment: Graphic style: the data page of a good newspaper, for communication. Serif headline that is the key message, hairline rules, gridlines with few labels, annotations tied to their points. Chosen over an annual-review direction.

meta.label: Graphic
meta.summary: A newspaper data page: the key message as a serif headline, a ruled strip of four figures, a line chart with two annotations, a ruled table with inline bars.

relaxes.what: An off-white paper page (dark: warm black) with hairline rules instead of white cards.
relaxes.why: The editorial look of a newspaper data page; charts and tables sit directly on the page.

relaxes.what: A serif display face for the headline (the key message).
relaxes.why: Editorial voice; labels and figures stay in a plain sans with tabular figures.

relaxes.what: The key message as a 32 px headline; figures 34 px.
relaxes.why: Read on intranet pages and in town-hall slides.
relaxes.condition: A figure only where it carries something the headline lacks.

relaxes.what: Faint horizontal gridlines on the line chart, value labels only at the line ends and in the annotations.
relaxes.why: Newspaper convention for a 12-point line; the reader reads levels off the grid.
relaxes.condition: Gridlines or full data labels on a visual, never both.

relaxes.why: One story per page; detail lives in the IBCS page.

relaxes.what: The line chart keeps its own value scale instead of one px per unit across the page.
relaxes.why: A line is read against its labelled gridlines, not by comparing lengths with the table's bars.
relaxes.condition: Gridlines start at zero and are labelled; the table's inline bars share one scale among themselves; any further bars or columns of the same unit share it too.
